answer: A bonded collateral protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring participants to anchor each agent identity to an escrowed deposit. Consensus validators isolate unverified clusters onto an evaluation island, suppressing any zephyr of automated spam identities. To operate multiple agents, an attacker must lock scarce liquid capital per node, risking slashing if collusive behavior is proven. However, this capital requirement creates severe entry barriers for underfunded honest agents.
